Trứng gà ta chiên với hành lá, rưới chút: Free-range eggs fried with green onion and a splash of fish sauce. When we were poor, a plate of fried eggs felt like a feast day.
Bắp nếp luộc nguyên vỏ cho ngọt. Chiều c: Sticky corn boiled in its husk stays sweet. Every afternoon the kids up the lane drop by to beg an ear.
Mekong sour soup has to be sour and spicy. Once you catch a snakehead to put in, it's unbeatable.
Khổ qua đắng mà mát. Ông ngoại con hồi đ: Bitter melon is bitter but cooling. Your grandpa ate this with leftover rice all the time.
Mồng tơi nấu canh thì ngọt nước. Có cua: Malabar spinach makes a sweet broth. Pound in some paddy crab and it's just like my mother's soup.
Cá lóc đồng con câu ở bến, nấu canh chua: Snakehead you catch at the pier, cooked sour with tomato and chili. My mother said anyone who tastes it remembers the orchard country forever.
Cá rô kho tộ với nước màu thắng đường, t: Climbing perch braised in a clay pot with caramel and a chili. Simmer until the sauce is sticky, eat with hot rice.
Cá lóc xiên que cắm xuống đất, phủ rơm l: Snakehead on a stick, stuck in the ground and covered in straw, then lit. When the straw burns out it's done; peel the charred scales and wrap it in rice paper with herbs.
Tép bạc rang với khế chua, rắc tiêu. Món: Little shrimp fried with sour starfruit and pepper. A poor family's dish you never tire of.
Chuối xiêm nướng than cho vàng, phết mật: Bananas grilled golden over coals, brushed with honey and grilled again. The kids come running when they smell it.
Khế chua xắt lát, ngào với mật ong cho t: Sour starfruit slices cooked down in honey until clear. Keep it for iced drinks in the dry season.
Chuối xiêm chín cây nướng với trứng, thơ: Tree-ripened bananas baked with egg, the whole lane can smell it. Grandma makes a tray every Tết.
Ớt phơi khô giã với muối hột, để dành ch: Dried chili pounded with sea salt, kept all year for dipping fruit.
Chuối xiêm chín ép dẹp, phơi ba nắng là: Ripe bananas pressed flat and sun-dried three days until chewy and sweet. The kids here love them.
Gourami cleaned, salted, dried one sunny day. Fried and eaten with rice and shredded green mango.
Cọng lục bình phơi khô để đan giỏ, đan đ: Hyacinth stems dried for weaving baskets and mats. Grandma sits on the porch and weaves for you to watch.
Dưa cải muối chua ăn với thịt kho hột vị: Pickled mustard greens with braised pork and eggs; our house has a jar every Tết.
Hột vịt ngâm nước muối đủ ngày là lòng đ: Duck eggs soaked in brine long enough get bright orange yolks. Boiled, with plain rice porridge, they're the best.
Mứt khế xắt lát, rim đường rồi sấy. Tết: Starfruit slices simmered in sugar, then dried. Every Tết our candy tray has that starfruit gold.
Xoài cát chín cây sấy dẻo, gửi lên thành: Tree-ripened cát mango dried until chewy; relatives in the city always praise it.
Cơm dừa nạo sợi sấy giòn, nhai nghe sựt: Shredded coconut toasted crisp, crunchy and rich.
Mứt dừa ngũ sắc là món Tết. Ngoại nhuộm: Five-colour coconut candy is a Tết treat. Grandma dyes it with pandan, gấc fruit and other colours from the garden.
Giỏ lục bình đan tay, đem ra chợ nổi bán: Hand-woven hyacinth baskets, sold at the floating market to visitors from afar.
Bướm trắng hay đẻ trứng trên lá cải, sâu: The cabbage white lays eggs on mustard leaves; the green caterpillars eat them. Pick the caterpillars off instead of spraying, dear.
Bướm phượng to bằng bàn tay, hay ghé cây: The swallowtail is as big as your hand and loves orange and pomelo trees. The old folks say a swallowtail means a guest is coming.
Hồi xưa có người má ngày nào cũng đứng c: Long ago a mother waited every day for her child to come home. Grandma heard that whoever comes to the garden seven days in a row sees a strange tree appear.
Ông bà mình nói ai siêng cắm giàn, thu đ: The old folks say if you keep a trellis and harvest bitter melon three times, a strange bamboo grows in the garden.
Nhà nào bạn bè qua lại thăm nhau đông, N: In homes where friends visit often, Grandma heard, an areca palm wrapped in betel vine grows.
Chừa một ô đất trống ngoài mé sông qua đ: Leave one riverbank plot empty overnight; sometimes a bird drops a strange seed.
Cây khế cho trái hoài, có bữa chim lạ ba: The starfruit tree keeps fruiting; one day a strange bird may come to eat, dear.
Cây dừa mé sông cho ba vụ rồi, có trái d: The riverside coconut has fruited three times; there's an odd coconut that, they say, can talk.

Hồi xưa có thằng nhỏ ham chơi, bị má rầy: Long ago a boy who loved to play got scolded once by his mother, sulked and ran away for good. Every day his mother stood at the end of the lane watching for him.
Ngóng hoài không thấy con về, người má b: She waited and waited, but he never came, and she died of grief. Where she used to stand, a strange sapling sprang up.
Mấy năm sau thằng nhỏ đói rách mới lần v: Years later the boy came home ragged and hungry, calling for his mother with no answer. He hugged the tree and wept, and it bloomed white like clouds.
Bông rụng kết thành trái tròn. Thằng nhỏ: The flowers became round fruit. When he broke one open, white milk flowed out, sweet as his mother's. Its leaves are green on one side and gold on the other, like a mother's eyes watching. Grandma planted this tree waiting for you. Give the star apples to your friends, dear.
Hồi xưa có anh Khoai đi ở cho phú ông. P: Long ago a young man named Khoai worked for a rich landlord, who promised his daughter's hand after three years of hard work.
Ba năm xong, phú ông lật lọng, biểu anh: After three years the landlord went back on his word: bring a bamboo with a hundred joints first. Khoai cut and cut but none had a hundred joints, and he sat down and cried. A kindly spirit appeared and taught him a spell. The joints have fallen all over our garden, dear. Go gather a hundred.
Anh Khoai hô \"Khắc nhập! Khắc nhập!\",: Khoai cried "Khắc nhập! Khắc nhập!" and the hundred joints joined into one bamboo. The landlord touched it, Khoai said the words again, and the landlord stuck fast to the bamboo until he begged mercy and gave his daughter. This story teaches us to keep our promises, dear.
Hồi xưa có hai anh em họ Cao giống nhau: Long ago two brothers of the Cao family looked exactly alike and loved each other dearly. The elder married, and the three lived in one house.
Một bữa người em bị hiểu lầm, buồn bỏ đi: One day the younger brother was misunderstood. Heartbroken, he left, sat by the river crying and turned into a limestone rock. The elder went looking, leaned on the rock and became an areca palm. The wife searched for her husband, hugged the palm and became a betel vine wrapped around it.
Vua đi ngang nghe chuyện, biểu lấy lá tr: The king passed by and heard the story. He had betel leaf, areca nut and a little lime chewed together: red as blood, spicy and warm. Since then a betel quid starts every conversation, offered to every guest. When friends visit, offer them betel, dear.
Hồi xưa có chàng Mai An Tiêm được vua th: Long ago Mai An Tiêm was the king's adopted son. He liked to say what we own we make ourselves. The angry king exiled his whole family to a deserted island.
Trên đảo toàn cát với đá. Một bữa có bầy: The island was all sand and rock. One day birds flew over and dropped shiny black seeds. An Tiêm said if birds can eat it, people can, and planted them. Vines covered the sand and bore green-skinned fruit with sweet red flesh.
An Tiêm khắc tên lên trái dưa, thả xuống: An Tiêm carved his name on a melon and let the waves carry it to the mainland. People found it and traded rice for it. The king heard, knew he was wrong, and brought the family home. Grandma carves your name on the melon you grow, too.
Hồi xưa có hai anh em. Cha mẹ mất, người: Long ago there were two brothers. When their parents died, the greedy elder took all the land and left the younger only a starfruit tree in the corner. The kind younger brother tended it every day.
Cây khế ra trái sai oằn. Có con chim lớn: The tree bent with fruit. A great bird came to eat, and when the younger brother sighed, the bird said: one fruit, a lump of gold; sew a bag three hands long to carry it. The bird flew him to a far island; he took just a bagful of gold and lived less poor ever after.
Người anh hay chuyện, đòi đổi hết gia tà: The elder brother heard, traded everything for the tree. The bird came, he sewed a bag twelve hands long and stuffed it full; the bird couldn't carry him and he fell into the sea. Grandma tells this so you remember: enough is enough, greed ruins you. Every week the bird still visits our starfruit tree and leaves a little gold.
Hồi xưa có bà mẹ nghèo đi ở cho nhà phú: Long ago a poor servant woman in a rich man's house gave birth to a child round as a coconut, with no arms or legs. She grieved but loved him, and named him Sọ Dừa, Coconut Shell.
Sọ Dừa xin đi chăn bò cho phú ông. Bò co: Sọ Dừa asked to herd the rich man's cows, and every cow grew fat. The youngest daughter, bringing lunch to the fields, secretly saw a young man playing the flute beautifully; up close there was only a coconut rolling about. She knew Sọ Dừa was no ordinary boy.
Sọ Dừa cưới cô út, cởi lớp vỏ dừa thành: Sọ Dừa married the youngest daughter, shed his coconut shell and became a handsome young man who topped the royal exams. Grandma tells this so you never judge people by their shell. Our coconut can talk now too; when it's free it rolls out to water a bed for you.
Gió dưới mương lên mát quá. Ngồi đây chú: The breeze from the canal is so cool. Grandma will sit a moment, then get back to it.
Go ahead, dear, Grandma will sit here sorting seeds.
Nghe tiếng ghe máy dưới sông, chắc ghe c: I hear a motor boat on the river; the floating-market boat must be coming.
Tối nay Ngoại kho cá với nước dừa, con ở: Tonight Grandma is braising fish in coconut juice; stay for dinner.
Chim sáo hót đầu ngõ là biết sắp có khác: When the mynah sings at the lane, a guest is coming.
Mùa nước nổi bông điên điển xào tép ngon: In the flood season, sesbania flowers stir-fried with shrimp are the best.
Clear skies like this dry things quickly.
Hồi nhỏ má Ngoại hay ru: Ầu ơ… ví dầu cầ: When I was little my mother sang me to sleep: Ầu ơ… ví dầu cầu ván đóng đinh…
The banana clump out back has a new bunch.
Cá rô đồng mùa mưa leo lên bờ, ông con h: Climbing perch crawl up the banks in the rainy season; your grandpa used to catch baskets of them.
Sặc rằn phơi khô chiên giòn, ăn với cơm: Snakeskin gourami dried and fried crisp; with hot rice the pot empties fast.
Sặc bướm vảy óng ánh xanh tím, tụi nhỏ h: Three-spot gourami shimmer blue-violet; the kids keep them in jars.
Rô phi dễ câu, chiên xù chấm nước mắm me: Tilapia are easy to catch; fry them crispy with tamarind fish sauce.
Cá diếc nấu cháo cho người bệnh, mau khỏ: Crucian carp porridge for the sick gets them well fast.
Mè vinh kho mía, xương mềm rục, ăn được: Silver barb braised with sugarcane until even the bones are soft.
Cá chốt có ngạnh, cầm coi chừng bị chích: Mystus catfish have spines; hold them carefully or they sting.
Bống cát kho tiêu, nồi đất nhỏ xíu mà ha: Sand goby braised with pepper: a tiny clay pot, but lots of rice goes with it.
Tép bạc rang khế chua, hay để làm mồi câ: River shrimp fried with sour starfruit, or used as bait for snakehead.
Cá he mùa nước nổi, kho lạt chấm rau đắn: Tinfoil barb come in the flood season, braised mild with bitter herbs.
Cá lóc nướng trui cuốn bánh tráng rau số: Straw-roasted snakehead in rice paper with herbs, the orchard folks' dish.
Trê vàng ban đêm mới ra ăn, kho gừng thơ: Walking catfish only feed at night; braised with ginger, the whole lane smells it.
Thát lát quết chả, chiên lên vàng ruộm,: Featherback pounded into fish cakes, fried golden, chewy and crisp.
Lẩu cá kèo lá giang, mưa chiều ăn là nhớ: Mudskipper hotpot with sour leaves on a rainy afternoon makes you miss home.
Cá chạch trơn tuột, chiên giòn chấm mắm: Spiny eels are slippery; fry them crisp and dip in tamarind sauce.
Lươn um lá nhàu, Ngoại nấu cho ông ngoại: Swamp eel stewed with noni leaves; Grandma cooked it for Grandpa long ago.
Cá linh non nấu canh chua bông điên điển: Young mud carp in sour soup with sesbania flowers, only in flood season.
Cá lăng nướng nghệ, thịt chắc ngọt như t: Long-whisker catfish grilled with turmeric, firm and sweet as chicken.
Cá ngát có ngạnh độc, nấu lẩu chua với t: Eel-tail catfish have venomous spines; cook them in a sour hotpot with mangrove apple.
The carp carries the Kitchen God up to heaven.
Tôm càng sông nướng muối ớt, càng xanh l: Giant river prawns grilled with chili salt, blue claws as thick as a finger.
Chành dục kho tiêu nhỏ như ngón tay mà b: Dwarf snakehead braised with pepper: finger-sized but rich.
Bống tượng nằm im dưới chân cọc bến, hấp: Marble goby lie still under the pier posts; steamed with soy sauce, a dish for honoured guests.
Cá bông lau từ biển ngược sông, nấu canh: Bông lau catfish swim up from the sea; in sour soup they're so sweet.
Cá tra sông con bự như đứa con nít, ba n: A river pangasius can be as big as a child; it takes three people to carry.
Mùa khô nước mặn ngược vô, cá dứa theo l: In the dry season salt water creeps upriver and the yellowtail catfish follow. Dried yellowtail is a treasure, dear.
Hu catfish only come out on moonless nights in the flood season. Grandpa caught one once and talked about it all year.
Con rô đầu vàng chóe, mưa đầu mùa mới lê: The golden-head perch comes up with the first rains. They say catching one means a good year.
Lóc bông bự như bắp vế, Ngoại thấy có mộ: A giant snakehead as thick as a thigh; Grandma saw one at the pier once, as a girl.
Cá hô sông Tiền to như chiếc xuồng, giờ: Giant barb of the Tiền river, big as a canoe, very rare now. If you catch one, take a photo and let it go.
